chapter_name: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the stagnant and backward state of the Indian economy in 1947, primarily caused by centuries of exploitative British colonial rule.

key_vocabulary.definition: A system where one country controls another, exploiting its resources for its own economic benefit.
A land revenue system where intermediaries (Zamindars) collected high rent from peasants regardless of crop yield.
The shift from cultivating crops for self-consumption to growing cash crops for sale in the market.
The deliberate destruction of India's world-famous handicraft industries by the British.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Under British rule, 85% of India's population lived in villages. Agriculture suffered from low productivity due to the exploitative Zamindari system, lack of irrigation, and forced commercialisation (growing indigo/cotton for British factories instead of food crops).

The British implemented a policy of 'systematic de-industrialisation'. They ruined India's famous handicraft sector by flooding the market with cheap, machine-made British goods while heavily taxing Indian exports. India was reduced to a mere exporter of raw materials.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🚢 Foreign Trade and Drain of Wealth
main_concepts.simple_explanation: India became a net exporter of raw materials (cotton, silk) and an importer of finished British goods. Though India had an export surplus, this wealth never benefited Indians; it was drained to pay for British administrative and war expenses.

The British built railways (1850), ports, and the telegraph system. However, the motive was not Indian development, but to easily transport raw materials to ports and effectively control the vast Indian territory.

fun_activity.title: 🚂 The Railway Paradox
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are an Indian weaver in 1860. The new railway line just reached your town! You think it will help you sell your cloth faster. But instead, the train brings thousands of cheap, machine-made British shirts that instantly put you out of business. This is how infrastructure was used as a tool for exploitation!

exam_tips: 📌 The 'Drain of Wealth' theory is a guaranteed question. Mention that the export surplus was used to pay for British colonial administration and wars, not for India's growth.
📌 Year of the Great Divide: 1921. Before 1921, India's population growth was fluctuating; after 1921, it grew continuously.
📌 Life expectancy was a mere 32 years (some sources say 44), and the literacy rate was less than 16%, highlighting extreme social backwardness.
quick_recap: ⭐ The primary motive of British rule was to turn India into a supplier of cheap raw materials and a consumer market for British finished goods.
⭐ The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 significantly reduced the transport cost and time between Britain and India, tightening British control.
⭐ The occupational structure remained stagnant, with over 70% of the workforce trapped in agriculture.
